steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Heat treatment alters material properties through controlled heating and cooling cycles without changing the shape. | Key Fact: Annealing heats metal above its critical temperature then cools it slowly (in the furnace) to soften and increase ductility. | Key Fact: Hardening heats steel above its critical temperature then quenches rapidly (in water or oil) to produce a hard, brittle martensitic structure. | Key Fact: Tempering reheats hardened steel to a lower temperature then cools it; reduces brittleness while retaining most of the hardness.
